question: Find the duration (in years) in which ₹1,200 will amount to ₹2,220 at a rate of 20% per annum simple interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Interest** earned = 2,220 − 1,200 = ₹1,020

**Interest** for 1 year = 20% of 1,200 = ₹240

Time (T) = Total Interest ÷ Yearly Interest

T = 1,020 ÷ 240 = 4.25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4.25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹1,200, Amount (A) = ₹2,220, Rate (R) = 20% p.a.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; Amount = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e6fa35a7c23da0ca6a4cc2c6d42f3056322d3c012808e5200b5a2d8d173e3b4.png] 

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = 2,220 − 1,200 = ₹1,020

⇒ 1,020 = (1,200 × 20 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,020 = 12 × 20 × T

⇒ 1,020 = 240 × T

⇒ T = 1,020 ÷ 240

⇒ T = 102 ÷ 24 = 4.25

**∴ The correct answer is 4.25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

**Simple Interest** is calculated only on the **Principal** amount, while **Compound Interest** is calculated on the Principal plus the accumulated Interest of previous periods.

Rule of 72

To find the approximate time required to **double** your money at a given annual interest rate (R), divide 72 by the rate: Time ≈ 72 ÷ R.

Amount Formula

The total **Amount** (A) at the end of the period is given by A = P × (1 + (R × T) ÷ 100) for **Simple Interest**.
